# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 5 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 5 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_005_page_001.jpg

---

5:1 Then the righteous will stand — unafraid, fully vindicated — before the very people who oppressed them and dismissed everything they lived for.

5:2 The sight of it will fill those people with dread. They will be shaken to the core by how completely unexpected his rescue was.

5:3 Sick with regret, in anguish of soul, they will groan and say to one another:

5:4 "This is the man we mocked. We made him into a joke, a shorthand for foolishness. What idiots we were. We said his life was insane and his death a disgrace.

5:5 And now he is counted among the children of God? How did his destiny end up with the holy ones?

5:6 We were the ones who went wrong. We walked away from truth. No light of righteousness ever found us. The sun never rose for us.

5:7 We exhausted ourselves on paths of lawlessness and ruin, wandering through deserts with no roads. We never once came to know the way of the Lord.

5:8 What did all our arrogance get us? What was the point of all that wealth we used to boast about?

5:9 Everything — gone. Like a shadow that disappears. Like news that flashes past and is instantly forgotten.

5:10 Like a ship pushing through a heaving sea, which leaves no trace behind when it passes — no furrow of its keel, no mark in the waves.

5:11 Or a bird in flight, cutting through air — when it has gone, nothing remains. The air, beaten by wings and split by the rush of feathers, seals itself back together. There is no sign it was ever there.

5:12 Or an arrow loosed toward its target — the air it splits closes immediately behind it. No one can trace where it went.

5:13 That is what we were. Born, and then almost immediately — gone. Not a single trace of virtue to show. Just consumed by our own wickedness."

5:14 The hope of the ungodly is chaff in a gust of wind. It is thin frost in a storm. It scatters like smoke before a breeze. It vanishes like the memory of a traveler who passed through for a single day.

5:15 But the righteous live forever. Their reward is held by the Lord. The Most High watches over them.

5:16 From his own hand they will receive a crown of glory and a diadem of beauty. His right hand will shelter them; his arm will be their shield.

5:17 He will arm himself with zeal — the whole armor of it. He will conscript all of creation to serve as his weapon against his enemies.

5:18 Righteousness becomes his breastplate. Justice — impartial, relentless — becomes his helmet.

5:19 Holiness becomes his invincible shield.

5:20 Fury becomes his sharpened sword. And creation stands at attention alongside him, ready to fight the reckless fools.

5:21 Bolts of lightning fly straight and sure, launched from the clouds toward their targets like arrows from a drawn bow.

5:22 Hailstones packed with fury are hurled like stones from a siege machine. Ocean waves surge over them. Rivers swallow them without mercy.

5:23 A mighty wind rises and blows them away like chaff. Lawlessness strips the whole earth bare. Evil tears down the thrones of kings.

---

*PNEUMA notes: The regret speech (vv. 3–13) is the dramatic payoff of chapter 2 — the same people who reasoned their way into nihilism now see clearly, but too late. The three-simile sequence (ship, bird, arrow) is given its own visual rhythm. The divine warfare passage (vv. 17–23) is rendered with military directness appropriate to its image-world — this passage is the conceptual source of Eph 6's "full armor of God."*
